b.answer:
Worked example: Tolu describes herself and Harvest Lane. (Phone is a sample number.)

{
  "name": "Tolu",
  "city": "Ibadan",
  "phone": "+2348000000000",
  "orders_per_day": 45,
  "delivers_on_sunday": false,
  "website": null,
  "business": { "name": "Harvest Lane", "type": "fresh-produce delivery", "riders": 4 },
  "products": ["tomatoes", "tatashe", "onions", "rodo"]
}

Features used: strings (name, city, phone), number (orders_per_day), boolean (delivers_on_sunday), null (website), nested object (business), array (products). Eight fields in total.

Paths checked in the lab:

  • business.name → "Harvest Lane" (string)
  • products[2] → "onions" (string; third item, counted from 0)
  • business.riders → 4 (number)

Why these types: the phone is a string so the country code and every digit are kept exactly; nobody will ever add two phone numbers together. orders_per_day is a number because it will be used in sums. delivers_on_sunday is a real boolean, not the text "no". The website is null on purpose: we know there isn't one, which is different from forgetting to fill it in.

A path that should fail: products[4] returns nothing, because the four products sit at positions 0 to 3.
mistakes: Storing the phone number as a number, or a count as a string like "45".
Using single quotes or leaving a trailing comma after the last field.
Writing products[3] for the third item instead of products[2].
Using an empty string "" where null was meant, so one of the six features is missing.
b.pass: Valid JSON with at least eight fields that includes a string, number, boolean, null, nested object and array, and three paths that each return the expected value in the lab.
b.redo: Send it back if the lab says invalid, any of the six features is missing, or a path returns nothing or the wrong item.

s.answer:
Worked example: three Harvest Lane orders. Prices: tomatoes ₦12,500, tatashe ₦9,000, onions ₦4,000, delivery ₦1,500.

[
 { "order_id": "HL-0043",
   "customer": { "name": "Mrs Adebayo", "phone": "+2348031234567" },
   "items": [ { "sku": "TOM-CRATE", "qty": 2, "unit_price": 12500 },
              { "sku": "PEP-TATASHE-L", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 9000 } ],
   "delivery_fee": 1500, "paid": true },
 { "order_id": "HL-0044",
   "customer": { "name": "Mr Okafor", "phone": "+2348059876543" },
   "items": [ { "sku": "ONI-BAG", "qty": 3, "unit_price": 4000 } ],
   "delivery_fee": 1500, "paid": false },
 { "order_id": "HL-0045",
   "customer": { "name": "Mrs Ade", "phone": "+2348067654321" },
   "items": [ { "sku": "TOM-CRATE", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 12500 },
              { "sku": "ONI-BAG", "qty": 2, "unit_price": 4000 },
              { "sku": "PEP-TATASHE-L", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 9000 } ],
   "delivery_fee": 1500, "paid": false }
]

Paths:

  • Second order's phone: [1].customer.phone → "+2348059876543"
  • Third item of the three-item order: [2].items[2].sku → "PEP-TATASHE-L"
  • Paid flags: [0].paid → true, [1].paid → false, [2].paid → false

Totals from paths:

OrderWorkingTotalPaid?
[0] HL-00432 × 12500 + 1 × 9000 + 150035500true
[1] HL-00443 × 4000 + 150013500false
[2] HL-00451 × 12500 + 2 × 4000 + 1 × 9000 + 150031000false

Unpaid grand total: 13500 + 31000 = 44500, shown to a person as ₦44,500.
mistakes: Starting paths at customer.phone instead of a position such as [1], when the whole JSON is an array.
Forgetting the delivery fee in one order's total, or adding the paid order to the unpaid total.
Pointing at items[3] for the third item.
Writing money as "₦12,500" or paid as "no", so the maths and the filter break.
s.pass: Valid JSON array of three orders (one with three items), paths that begin with a position and return the right values in the lab, each order's total worked from paths, and a correct unpaid total.
s.redo: Send it back if the JSON doesn't validate, paths skip the top-level position, a total leaves out the fee, or the unpaid total includes a paid order.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's Open-Meteo response from 0.2 (Ibadan, three days; your numbers will differ).

#PathValue
1latitude7.375
2longitude3.9375
3timezone"Africa/Lagos"
4daily_units.precipitation_probability_max"%"
5daily_units.precipitation_sum"mm"
6daily.time[0]"2026-10-01"
7daily.time[1]"2026-10-02"
8daily.precipitation_probability_max[1]70
9daily.precipitation_sum[1]6.1
10daily.time[2]"2026-10-03"

Flattening: one tab, Forecast_Days, one row per day. The daily lists line up by position, so row n takes position n from each list.

daterain_chance_pctrain_mmlatitudelongitude
2026-10-01350.47.3753.9375
2026-10-02706.17.3753.9375
2026-10-03200.07.3753.9375

Units go in the column names (pct, mm), not in the cells, so every cell holds one plain value. date stays an ISO string, rain_chance_pct and rain_mm are numbers, so a later step can filter "rain_chance_pct is 50 or more". The location columns repeat on every row; that's fine, because each row must make sense on its own. If you call the holidays API instead, the body is already a list of objects, so it flattens to one row per holiday with columns date, localName and name.

Same paths in n8n and Make (Make counts from 1; 1. is the module number):

n8n  {{ $json.daily.time[0] }}
Make {{get(1.daily.time; 1)}}

n8n  {{ $json.daily.precipitation_probability_max[1] }}
Make {{get(1.daily.precipitation_probability_max; 2)}}

n8n  {{ $json.daily.precipitation_sum[2] }}
Make {{get(1.daily.precipitation_sum; 3)}}

Submit: the pasted response, the 10 paths with lab results, the table design and the three path pairs.
mistakes: Flattening into one row with columns day1, day2, day3, or a list inside a single cell.
Copying n8n positions straight into Make without adding one.
Fewer than three paths inside arrays, or paths that only work on their own typed-up copy rather than the real response.
Putting units like "70%" or "6.1 mm" inside cells instead of in the column name.
g.pass: Ten paths that all return values in the lab from a real pasted response (at least three inside arrays), a table design with one row per day and no lists in cells, and three paths written in both syntaxes with Make shifted up by one.
g.redo: Send it back if any path fails in the lab, the design stores lists in cells or one column per day, or the Make positions aren't shifted.
